facts.fact: The StackAdapt blog article 'Embracing contextual vs. behavioural targeting' was published on 29 March 2021.
According to StackAdapt, behavioural targeting has been widely used in online advertising for over a decade.
facts.quote: This targeting method has been widely used in online advertising for over a decade.

facts.fact: According to StackAdapt, cookies have made tracking in-browser user behaviour a valuable targeting tool since the 1990s.
facts.quote: Since the 1990s, the cookie has made tracking in-browser user behaviour a valuable tool for targeting digital ads toward receptive consumers.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that some browsers are phasing out 3rd-party cookie tracking, which will make behavioural advertising more restricted in coming years.
facts.quote: Some browsers are phasing out 3rd-party cookie tracking.

facts.fact: StackAdapt lists four reasons why contextual targeting is effective and beneficial.
facts.quote: Here are 4 reasons why contextual targeting is both effective and beneficial:

facts.fact: StackAdapt describes behavioural targeting as also called audience targeting or demographic targeting, which serves ads based on a user's web-browsing behaviour collected via a tracking pixel or cookie.
facts.quote: Behavioural targeting, often referred to as audience targeting or demographic targeting, aims to ensure that an ad is relevant to the user visiting a page.

facts.fact: StackAdapt describes contextual advertising as targeting ad placements using algorithms based on keywords, website content, and other metadata rather than user behaviour.
facts.quote: This targeting method uses algorithms to target ad placements based on keywords, website content, and other metadata.

facts.fact: Contextual advertising works based on a crawler that crawls the web and records information on each web page, which the DSP then matches against campaign context.
facts.quote: Contextual advertising works based on a crawler.

facts.fact: Behavioural targeting uses hard, historical data of user browsing patterns to display ads.
facts.quote: Behavioural targeting uses hard, historical data of user browsing patterns to display ads.

facts.fact: Contextual targeting focuses on the content of the page a user is browsing, reading, or watching at the current moment.
facts.quote: Contextual targeting focuses on the content of the page a user is browsing, reading, or watching at the current moment.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that contextual advertising provides a high-performing targeting solution that does not require the use of cookies (vendor claim, no figures given).
facts.quote: Contextual advertising provides a high performing targeting solution that does not require the use of cookies.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that it is still impossible to predict human behaviour 100% of the time, even with the growing amount of online data collected daily (vendor's own claim).
facts.quote: it’s still impossible to 100% predict human behaviour.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that leveraging AI lets a contextual campaign pick up variations of the primary target term, known as semantic keywords, to appear in related articles.
facts.quote: Leveraging AI allows your contextual campaign to pick up on variations of your primary target term, known as semantic keywords

facts.fact: StackAdapt recommends using both contextual and behavioural targeting in a campaign strategy rather than choosing one (vendor recommendation).
facts.quote: the short answer is you should be using both.
